record.paper_title: Open Problems About Sumsets in Finite Abelian Groups: Minimum Sizes and Critical Numbers
record.context_brief: Sharpness of lower bounds for restricted 3-critical numbers
record.original_question: For the cyclic group Z_n, define the restricted 3-fold sumset 3^A of a subset A as the set of all sums of three distinct elements of A. Define the restricted 3-critical number χ^(Z_n,3) as the least integer m such that 3^A=Z_n for every m-element subset A of Z_n. Are the following lower bounds always sharp for n≥16? If n has a prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3 and p is the smallest such divisor, then χ^(Z_n,3) should equal (1+1/p)n/3+3 when n=p, (1+1/p)n/3+2 when n=3p, and (1+1/p)n/3+1 otherwise. If n has no prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3, then χ^(Z_n,3) should equal floor(n/3)+4 when 9 divides n and floor(n/3)+3 otherwise.

evidence.quote: the h-fold restricted sumset: hˆA = {Σ_i=1^m λ_i ai | λ1,...,λm ∈ {0, 1}, Σ_i=1^m λi = h}
Given G and h, we define the h-critical number χ (G, h) as the least integer m for which hA = G holds for all m-subsets A of G; we define χˆ(G, h) and χ± (G, h) analogously.
We also believe that, actually, equality holds above for all n—this is certainly the case if n is even or prime; we have verified this (by computer) for all n ≤ 50.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_n$ denote the cyclic group of order $n$. For a subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_n$, define the restricted 3-fold sumset
$$3^\wedge A=\{a_1+a_2+a_3 : a_1,a_2,a_3\in A,\ a_1,a_2,a_3\text{ pairwise distinct}\}.$$
Define the restricted 3-critical number $\chi^\wedge(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)$ as the least integer $m$ such that for every subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_n$ with $|A|=m$, one has $3^\wedge A=\mathbb{Z}_n$.

Determine whether, for every integer $n\ge 16$, the following equalities hold:

(I) If $n$ has a prime divisor congruent to $2\pmod 3$, and $p$ is the smallest such divisor, then
$$\chi^\wedge(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)=\begin{cases}\left(1+\tfrac1p\right)\tfrac{n}{3}+3 & \text{if }n=p,\\[2pt] \left(1+\tfrac1p\right)\tfrac{n}{3}+2 & \text{if }n=3p,\\[2pt] \left(1+\tfrac1p\right)\tfrac{n}{3}+1 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

(II) If $n$ has no prime divisor congruent to $2\pmod 3$, then
$$\chi^\wedge(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)=\begin{cases}\lfloor n/3\rfloor+4 & \text{if }9\mid n,\\ \lfloor n/3\rfloor+3 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

That is, prove or disprove that the stated lower bounds for $\chi^\wedge(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)$ are sharp for all $n\ge 16$.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on critical numbers for restricted sumsets in finite abelian groups (2026) discusses the restricted 3-critical number for cyclic groups, noting that the conjectured exact value matches a lower bound and generalizes a conjecture of Gallardo–Grekos et al. proved by Lev for large n. The full sharpness conjecture for all n ≥ 16 in Z_n does not appear to be established; the question appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Critical Numbers for Restricted Sumsets: Rigidity and Collapse in Finite Abelian Groups
status_evidence.snippet: A lower bound is provided for the restricted 3-critical number in cyclic groups Z_n—conjectured to be exact for every n—which is a generalization of a conjecture made by Gallardo, Grekos, et al. that was proved (for large n) by Lev.
status_evidence.claim: The exact value of the restricted 3-critical number for all Z_n remains conjectural; sharpness has been established only for large n or special cases.
